purpose: Optional source directory for finding and verifying evidence while drafting coin companion enrichment. Source entries are leads, not evidence; open and verify the relevant source before relying on it.
use_rules: Start with the supplied catalog object and current enrichment draft; research only claims needed for the visitor-facing writeup.
Start with the coin's own catalogue reference, then prefer a primary text, standard catalogue, or specialist numismatic database that directly covers the claim.
Use this package as a shortlist, not as evidence. Browse the relevant source page, record, text, or scan and verify the exact support for each factual claim.
A source title, URL, or listed status is not evidence by itself. Do not cite a source unless its relevant content was opened and checked.
Period routes are starting points, not complete coverage. Search directly for a more specific specialist source when needed; do not treat a general source as a coin-type authority.
Do not use search snippets, auction descriptions, dealer prices, or acquisition data as evidence.
After two failed attempts to access a source for a claim, stop retrying; use another source, qualify the claim from available evidence, or omit it.
Keep temporary claim-to-source notes in the chat or working draft. No separate facts ledger or source registry is required.
Use primary or standard references for strong claims; qualify claims based only on secondary or fallback sources; omit unsupported or contradicted claims.

source_lanes.purpose: Confirm attribution, type, legend, date, mint, denomination, and catalogue-reference variants.
source_lanes.priority_note: Use the coin's own named catalogue reference first when available. Use Wildwinds as a cross-check or lead; its specimen weights are tier B and must not be lifted from auction descriptions.

source_lanes.purpose: Find primary textual context for named rulers, events, titles, religious references, and motifs.
source_lanes.priority_note: Use the exact work, book, and chapter locator. Open the text itself; do not infer a passage from a site's general coverage.

source_lanes.purpose: Check Jewish texts, biblical passages, and relevant provincial coin types.
source_lanes.priority_note: Separate a text's date and genre from the date of the coin. The Meshorer entry is a lead to a lending copy, not a directly read source.

source_lanes.purpose: Support monetary-system, metal, wage, price, tax, and relative-purchasing-power claims.
source_lanes.priority_note: Record the place, date, unit, and source for each number. Use relative comparisons only; do not convert to modern currency. Treat OCR and reconstructed series cautiously and record the calculation or estimate basis.

source_lanes.purpose: Cross-check individual specimens, object metadata, and accessible catalogue scans.
source_lanes.priority_note: The British Museum and Dumbarton Oaks sites have recorded scripted-fetch 403 errors. Use the specified open catalogue scans when available; do not assume a landing page was read.

source_lanes.purpose: Orient a claim about a ruler, city, or historical sequence before checking it against stronger evidence.
source_lanes.priority_note: These are secondary/fallback leads, not substitutes for a primary text or standard coin catalogue. Keep claims hedged at tier B unless independently supported.

sources.title: Roman Provincial Coinage Online (RPC)
sources.use_for: Provincial types, dating, metal, average diameter and average weight; especially Judaea, Alexandria, Balkan, and Anatolian mints.
sources.access_note: Locate and open the specific coin type record. Denomination and fineness are not consistently supplied.

sources.title: Online Coins of the Roman Empire (OCRE)
sources.use_for: RIC type identifiers, dates, and reported average weights and diameters for Roman imperial coinage.
sources.access_note: Registry has recorded intermittent 503 responses; if a type page fails, use a listed alternate and record the failure.

sources.title: Catalogue of the Byzantine Coins in the Dumbarton Oaks Collection and in the Whittemore Collection (DOC), vols. 1, 3.2, 4
sources.use_for: Byzantine types, dates, monetary reforms, denominations, and selected metrology across DOC volumes 1, 3.2, and 4.
sources.access_note: Use registry volume-specific scan/text patterns. OCR tables can be scrambled; verify readings against the scan.

sources.title: D. M. Metcalf, Coinage of the Crusades and the Latin East in the Ashmolean Museum, Oxford (RNS Special Publication 15, 1983)
sources.use_for: Crusader and Latin East coinage, including Antioch and Cyprus types, references, and catalogue weights.
sources.access_note: The open OCR is useful but can garble numerals; confirm a consequential number against the printed page.

sources.title: Walker, Catalogue of the Muhammadan Coins in the British Museum (vol. 1, 1941, Arab-Sassanian) and Catalogue of the Arab-Byzantine and Post-Reform Umaiyad Coins (vol. 2, 1956)
sources.use_for: Early Islamic and Arab-Byzantine coinage, reform chronology, metrology, and catalogue context.
sources.access_note: Registry covers open text files and OCR limits; introduction-level metrology is more reliable than scrambled catalogue tables.

sources.title: Wildwinds
sources.use_for: Broad type descriptions, references, and cross-checking across ancient and medieval series.
sources.access_note: Secondary lead only. Specimen weights are tier B; never use auction descriptions, dealer prices, or linked sale information.

sources.title: Corpus Nummorum
sources.use_for: Greek civic coin types, especially Thrace and Moesia.
sources.access_note: Registry has not verified a specific type page or weight; use only after opening the relevant record.

sources.title: Berlin Münzkabinett (IKMK)
sources.use_for: Museum specimen records, object weights, and catalogue references.
sources.access_note: This is a source lead only. Locate and inspect the specific object record before citing.

sources.title: Seleucid Coins Online (SCO)
sources.use_for: Seleucid type attribution and chronology, alongside Houghton and Lorber references.
sources.access_note: Known 503 responses; treat as unavailable until the specific type page is opened.

sources.title: Ptolemaic Coins Online (PCO)
sources.use_for: Ptolemaic type attribution and chronology, alongside Lorber references.
sources.access_note: Known 503 responses for the root and a sample record; treat as unavailable until the specific type page is opened.

sources.title: Perseus Digital Library
sources.use_for: Greek and Latin primary texts, including Polybius, Pliny, Suetonius, Josephus, Livy, and Plutarch.
sources.access_note: Use exact work/chapter references; registry lists absent works and passages that did not resolve.

sources.title: LacusCurtius, Penelope (Bill Thayer)
sources.use_for: Roman and Byzantine-era authors including Suetonius, Cassius Dio, Herodian, Procopius, and Ammianus.
sources.access_note: Recent connections to some pages failed or timed out; confirm live access and use the exact work locator.

sources.title: Wikisource
sources.use_for: Tacitus, Lactantius, Procopius, and other open historical texts.
sources.access_note: Registry lists available texts and known absent works; cite the work, book, and chapter.

sources.title: New Advent, Church Fathers
sources.use_for: Eusebius, Lactantius, Irenaeus, Sozomen, and Ambrose, including Life of Constantine.
sources.access_note: Use a specific book and chapter, and confirm the passage is present on the page you opened.

sources.title: Internet History Sourcebooks (Fordham)
sources.use_for: Byzantine and Crusader-era sources, including Anna Komnene and First Crusade chronicles.
sources.access_note: Some pages fail or omit the relevant passage; open the cited translation and locate the exact passage.

sources.title: Attalus
sources.use_for: Hellenistic and Roman source excerpts.
sources.access_note: This is a source lead only. Verify the exact source passage before use.

sources.title: Sefaria (Mishnah, Tosefta, Talmud)
sources.use_for: Judaean monetary, wage, price, and tax context in named Jewish texts.
sources.access_note: Open the relevant text and identify its edition or translation; do not conflate versions or commentary.

sources.title: bible-api.com
sources.use_for: Specific biblical passages about wages, prices, taxes, and coin references.
sources.access_note: Identify the translation used and record the exact book, chapter, and verse.

sources.title: Diocletian, Edict on Maximum Prices (Kent 1920, Allen 2007, Abbott 1911, Mommsen 1851 readings)
sources.use_for: The 301 CE price and wage schedule and its preamble.
sources.access_note: Record the edition or reading and line or item number; check for variant readings and missing text.

sources.title: Hendy, Studies in the Byzantine Monetary Economy c. 300-1450 (Cambridge, 1985)
sources.use_for: Byzantine monetary reforms, weights, metal fineness, wage/pay context, and denomination relationships.
sources.access_note: Large OCR text has number and fraction errors; confirm important figures against the cited printed page/table.

sources.title: Morrisson and Cheynet, Prices and Wages in the Byzantine World, in Laiou (ed.), The Economic History of Byzantium (Dumbarton Oaks, 2002), ch. 12, pp. 815-871
sources.use_for: Byzantine price and wage evidence, with period-specific references.
sources.access_note: Locate the exact item and page in the collection; this landing URL alone is not a passage locator.

sources.title: Global Price and Income History Group (UC Davis)
sources.use_for: Published historical wage and price series, including Istanbul, Sopron, and Vienna datasets.
sources.access_note: Name the dataset, place, date range, and units. Do not equate a series directly with an individual coin's purchasing power.

sources.title: Papyri.info
sources.use_for: Documentary evidence for Egyptian wages, prices, tax receipts, and pay statements.
sources.access_note: Registry reports an anti-bot challenge on sampled pages; no claim is supported until the document itself is read.

sources.title: Internet Archive
sources.use_for: Open scans and text editions of specialist catalogues and scholarly works.
sources.access_note: Access varies by item; many listed books are borrow-only. Verify the specific item, edition, and page.

sources.title: British Museum collection online
sources.use_for: Individual museum specimen records and object metadata.
sources.access_note: Registry reports 403 to scripted fetches; do not treat an unvisited record as verified.

sources.title: Dumbarton Oaks Byzantine coins resources
sources.use_for: DOC catalogue orientation and Byzantine coin resources.
sources.access_note: Registry reports 403; use the relevant Internet Archive DOC scan and follow its volume-specific access notes.

sources.title: Livius.org
sources.use_for: Ruler, place, and chronology orientation for the ancient world.
sources.access_note: Secondary context only; some person URLs return incomplete pages. Confirm factual claims with a stronger source.

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica (Wayback copies)
sources.use_for: Fallback ruler and place summaries where stronger sources are unavailable.
sources.access_note: Find the exact archived article and snapshot. Direct Britannica access and some archived articles fail.

sources.title: Meshorer, Ancient Jewish Coinage and A Treasury of Jewish Coins
sources.use_for: Hasmonean, Herodian, and prefect coin types and denomination references.
sources.access_note: Registry records a lending copy that was not opened; do not cite claims from this entry without reading the relevant pages.

sources.title: Wikipedia
sources.use_for: Last-resort orientation or a fallback claim when no better source is reachable.
sources.access_note: Use only after trying a primary or standard source; open the article text, verify the cited material, and hedge at tier B.
